messages:
lina: quick check — customer private cluster (on-prem v2) showing ~10% p95 regressed vs hosted for long-context streaming. can someone help validate parity and rule out infra config? tagging @jason @kevin @nori :wave

jason: can you paste the failing perf numbers and the exact bench command you ran?

lina: p50 120ms, p95 462ms, throughput ~18k tok/s for redwood-7b @ seq=2048, concurrency=4. bench command we used:```./run_bench.sh --model redwood-7b --seq 2048 --concurrency 4 --mode streaming --samples 200 --host private-cluster-01```

kevin: a few quick suspects: MTU/body fragmentation, NIC offloads, NUMA pinning, and any difference in hugepages or kernel net.core buffers. also check flow-control/RDMA (RoCE) if they're using that.

nori: +1. also confirm we run same quantization artifacts and runtime build (AVX vs AMX kernels). sometimes the onprem AMI lacked our latest kernel flags.

perf-bot: upload complete — attached artifacts: perf-1769456789.tar.gz (latency hist, flamegraph, perf stat). summary: cycles and cache-misses elevated on private nodes during KV cache refill.

jason: can someone run this quick checklist on a repro node and paste results?
- output of `uname -a`
- `ethtool -k eth0`
- `ip link show eth0` (MTU)
- `numactl --hardware`
- `cat /proc/meminfo | grep Huge`
- `sudo perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses -p <pid> -- sleep 30`

kevin: also run a bench with MTU bumped to 9000 and with NIC offloads toggled off to see delta. sometimes fragmentation adds ~50-100us per RPC which compounds.

lina: i'll coordinate with customer next hour. jason/nori — who can run the `perf stat` and the MTU test?

jason: i can run the MTU + bench now. will report in ~20m.

nori: i'll do perf stat and check hugepages + numa. ping me if you need kernel tunables changed.

(20m later)
jason: ran with MTU 9000, same bench. p95 dropped from 462ms -> 378ms. throughput up ~8%. logs: `bench-1769456920.log` (uploaded).

nori: perf stat results: cycles 2.4e11 -> 1.9e11 (after NIC tuning), cache-misses down 18%. HugePages not enabled on these nodes. numactl shows memory interleaved across 2 NUMA nodes, CPUs pinned to all sockets.

kevin: that suggests two things: enable hugepages + ensure process pinned to local NUMA node for GPU affinity. also we should standardize AMI to set MTU 9000 and tweak `net.core.rmem_max`/`wmem_max`. example sysctl to try:```sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=134217728 net.core.wmem_max=134217728 vm.nr_hugepages=1024```

lina: great. action items: 1) jason to run one bench with hugepages enabled + NUMA-local cpuset. 2) infra to bake MTU=9000 + sysctl into our private AMI. 3) perf team to update the regression dashboard with this private vs hosted comparison. i'll open INF-789 to track.

jason: running hugepages + cpuset now, will post numbers.

perf-bot: note — add test to daily parity job: long-context streaming seq=2048 for redwood-7b. threshold p95 delta <= 5%.

(15m later)
jason: hugepages + cpuset run complete: p95 355ms, throughput +12% vs baseline. so most of delta explained by MTU + hugepages + NUMA pinning.

lina: perfect, thanks team. can we get infra to schedule AMI update this week? also let's add a short runbook entry under docs/private-deploy/perf-parity.md with the checklist: MTU, offloads, hugepages, numa pinning, kernel buf tunables, runtime build hash.

infra-bot: created ticket INF-790 for AMI bake with MTU/hugepages config and INF-789 created for parity dashboard. ETA: 3 business days.

kevin: once AMI baked, let's rerun the parity harness and close the loop. :+1:

lina: thanks everyone — closing this thread after infra confirms bake.
